text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Hezbollah member helped CSIS: Deportee provided security service with evidence group set up operations base in Canada.
- Cost cuts killing legal aid, study says: Law body urged to give up control.
- UN to airlift Hutus from Zaire: Rebel leader approves mission: peace talks move to secret location in South Africa.
- No hot buttons in Chretien visit: Canada-U.S. irritants take second place to global topics.
- Villagers doubt gold at end of rainbow.
- New links seen for Eaton chain: Retailer likely to survive but much slimmer and without family at the helm, observers say.
- Cash-rich TrizecHahn on a roll: Firm confident it can juggle flurry of deals.
- What went wrong at Money Growth: Fund dealer's act led to shortfall.
- Play waiting game on junior miners, analysts advise.
- Bre-X haunted by spectre of 'salting': Rumors swirl around possibility that ore samples from Busang were tampered with and gold was added from another source.
- Greyhound gives airline deadline to make profit.
